claim: Exact hash-bound mechanical source normalizations for the pinned direct Flyspeck route

entries.semantic_rule: In pinned OCaml 4.14.1, Stdlib maps == to %eq, translprim maps %eq to Pintcomp Ceq, and structural = on int also specializes to Pintcomp Ceq; the runtime representation additionally encodes each int injectively as one tagged immediate word. The two predicates therefore select the same branch for every int value.
entries.scope_limit: This scalar rule does not apply to allocated values and does not authorize changing any identity-sensitive list comparison.

operations.after:
let partition p l =
  let rec part l =
    match l with
      [] -> [],[],true,true
    | h::t ->
        let yes,no,all_yes,all_no = part t in
        if p(h) then
          ((if all_yes then l else h::yes),no,all_yes,false)
        else
          (yes,(if all_no then l else h::no),false,all_no) in
  let yes,no,_,_ = part l in yes,no;;

let qmap _ _ =
  failwith "Candle Flyspeck: qmap requires physical sharing observation";;

operations.before:
let undefine =
  let rec undefine_list x l =
    match l with
      (a,b as ab)::t ->
          let c = Stdlib.compare x a in
          if c = 0 then t
          else if c < 0 then l else
          let t' = undefine_list x t in
          if t' == t then l else ab::t'
    | [] -> [] in
  fun x ->
    let k = Hashtbl.hash x in
    let rec und t =
      match t with
        Leaf(h,l) when h = k ->
          let l' = undefine_list x l in
          if l' == l then t
          else if l' = [] then Empty
          else Leaf(h,l')
      | Branch(p,b,l,r) when k land (b - 1) = p ->
          if k land b = 0 then
            let l' = und l in
            if l' == l then t
            else (match l' with Empty -> r | _ -> Branch(p,b,l',r))
          else
            let r' = und r in
            if r' == r then t
            else (match r' with Empty -> l | _ -> Branch(p,b,l,r'))
      | _ -> t in
    und;;
operations.after:
let undefine =
  let rec undefine_list_changed x l =
    match l with
      (a,b as ab)::t ->
          let c = Stdlib.compare x a in
          if c = 0 then Some t
          else if c < 0 then None else
          (match undefine_list_changed x t with
             None -> None
           | Some t' -> Some(ab::t'))
    | [] -> None in
  fun x ->
    let k = Hashtbl.hash x in
    let rec und_changed t =
      match t with
        Leaf(h,l) when h = k ->
          (match undefine_list_changed x l with
             None -> None
           | Some l' ->
               Some(if l' = [] then Empty else Leaf(h,l')))
      | Branch(p,b,l,r) when k land (b - 1) = p ->
          if k land b = 0 then
            (match und_changed l with
               None -> None
             | Some l' ->
                 Some(match l' with Empty -> r
                                    | _ -> Branch(p,b,l',r)))
          else
            (match und_changed r with
               None -> None
             | Some r' ->
                 Some(match r' with Empty -> l
                                    | _ -> Branch(p,b,l,r')))
      | _ -> None in
    fun t -> match und_changed t with None -> t | Some t' -> t';;

entries.semantic_rule: The filter, partition, uniq, and Patricia-tree undefine rewrites carry an explicit changed/all-unchanged result instead of observing physical identity, preserving structural results, callback order, exception order, and the original unchanged object whenever the source did. The exact selected graph has no qmap caller outside its recursive definition, so the normalized binding fails closed if a missed dynamic or future call reaches it.
entries.scope_limit: qmap is a selected-graph non-use refinement, not general qmap compatibility; final full-run fingerprints, performance measurements, and a compiled normalized-source run remain release gates.

entries.semantic_rule: The filter is used only to construct the avoidance set passed to mk_primed_var. Structural exclusion removes every occurrence equal to the abstraction binder. For separately allocated equal variable nodes this can choose a less-primed binder than OCaml's physical filter, but relabel_bound_conv still returns an alpha-equivalent theorem; the exact selected-run fingerprint must determine whether even the binder spelling is unchanged.
entries.scope_limit: The rule is specific to relabel_bound_conv and its fresh-name consumer; it does not authorize replacing physical identity by structural equality elsewhere. A compiled theorem/output oracle and final fingerprint remain required, and any exact-fingerprint difference blocks release.
